title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1960
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 1960 with the song "Bonne nuit ma chérie", composed by Franz Josef Breuer, with lyrics by Kurt Schwabach, and performed by Wyn Hoop. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Hessischer Rundfunk, selected its entry through a national final.

title: 5 July - 10th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 10th annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 24 June to 5 July 1960. The Golden Bear was awarded to El Lazarillo de Tormes directed by César Fernández Ardavín.

title: “Marina” by Rocco Granata
text: Rocco Granata is an Italian-Belgian singer, songwriter, and accordionist. Granata was born in Figline Vegliaturo, Calabria, southern Italy; but his parents immigrated to Belgium when he was aged ten.

title: “Wir wollen niemals auseinandergehn” by Heidi Brühl
text: Heidi Rosemarie Brühl was a German singer and actress who came to prominence as a young teenager and had a prolific career in film and television. She was also a successful recording artist, and is known for her participation in the Eurovision Song Contest 1963.

title: “Milord” by Dalida
text: "Milord" or "Ombre de la Rue" ("Shadow of the Street") is a 1959 song (lyrics by Georges Moustaki, music by Marguerite Monnot), famously sung by Édith Piaf.

title: “Die Liebe ist ein seltsames Spiel” by Connie Francis
text: Concetta Rosa Maria Franconero, known professionally as Connie Francis, was an American singer and actress. One of the top-charting female vocalists of the late 1950s and early 1960s, she amassed over 200 million records sold, placing her among the best-selling music artists in history.
listen: Die Liebe ist ein seltsames Spiel Connie Francis

title: “Ein Schiff wird kommen” by Lale Andersen
text: "Never on Sunday", also known by its original Greek title "Ta Pediá tou Pireá", is a song written by Manos Hatzidakis and first sung by Melina Mercouri in the film of the same name, directed by Jules Dassin and starring Mercouri. The song won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 1960, a first for a foreign-language picture.
listen: Ein Schiff wird kommen Lale Andersen

title: “Ramona” by Blue Diamonds
text: "Ramona" is a 1928 song with lyrics by L. Wolfe Gilbert and music by Mabel Wayne. Composed for the 1928 feature film Ramona, it was the first theme song written for the movies.
